title: Indian Railways Approves ₹233 Crore for Electronic Interlocking at 21 Stations in Samastipur Division
subtitle: Modern Electronic Interlocking System to Strengthen Signalling Infrastructure and Support Kavach Implementation
body_text:
Indian Railways has approved the provision of Electronic Interlocking (EI) at 21 stations of Samastipur Division of East Central Railway (ECR) at a total cost of ₹233 crore.
Modernisation of Signalling Infrastructure at 21 Stations
The approved work involves replacement of existing Panel Interlocking with Electronic Interlocking at 21 stations of Samastipur Division. The modern signalling system will strengthen railway signalling infrastructure across the division and facilitate the implementation of Kavach, the indigenous Automatic Train Protection system.
Strengthening Railway Safety and Operational Efficiency
The provision of Electronic Interlocking will modernise the signalling arrangements at the identified stations and provide a more advanced signalling infrastructure in connection with Kavach works.
Electronic Interlocking is a modern signalling technology that replaces ageing relay-based systems with computer-based interlocking, ensuring higher reliability, faster fault diagnosis, easier maintenance and enhanced operational flexibility.
The initiative is part of Indian Railways’ continued efforts towards modernisation of signalling systems, strengthening railway safety and enhancing operational efficiency across its network.
*****
Mahesh Kumar/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj

enrichment.summary: Indian Railways has sanctioned ₹233 crore to replace the existing Panel Interlocking system with modern Electronic Interlocking (EI) at 21 stations in the Samastipur Division of East Central Railway. The upgrade will modernise signalling infrastructure and support the rollout of Kavach, India's indigenous Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system, at these stations.
enrichment.context: Electronic Interlocking is a computer-based signalling technology that is replacing older relay-based Panel Interlocking systems across Indian Railways, offering better reliability, faster fault diagnosis and easier maintenance. Its deployment is a prerequisite for implementing Kavach, the Research Design and Standards Organisation (RDSO)-developed indigenous Automatic Train Protection system that automatically applies brakes to prevent train collisions, especially in cases of signal overshoot or driver error. Kavach gained heightened public and policy attention after recent train accidents renewed focus on railway safety, and the government has been expanding its coverage across high-density and other routes as part of a broader safety modernisation drive. This particular sanction is one of many divisional-level infrastructure upgrades being rolled out to enable pan-India Kavach implementation, reflecting the incremental but steady pace of signalling modernisation on Indian Railways.

options: An indigenous Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system developed to prevent train collisions
A satellite-based train tracking system for freight logistics
A biometric attendance system for railway staff
A financial audit software used by Indian Railways
prelims_questions.explanation: Kavach is an indigenous Automatic Train Protection system developed by RDSO that automatically applies brakes to prevent collisions caused by signal overshooting or human error.

prelims_questions.question: Electronic Interlocking (EI), as referred to in Indian Railways signalling modernisation, is primarily meant to replace which older system?
options: Panel Interlocking based on relay technology
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that EI replaces the existing relay-based Panel Interlocking system, offering higher reliability and easier maintenance.
